name: Group C executed TypeScript crosscheck
rule: Every value below was returned by a function in reference/mochimo-wots, and every input was read from group_c_addr.json or a sidecar it names. Nothing here is transcribed and nothing is hand-computed. Regenerate rather than edit.

oracle.why: Two implementations of one algorithm, and they can disagree. The C in reference/mochimo-core computed the values in group_c_addr.json; the TypeScript in reference/mochimo-wots computed the values here, from the same inputs, and neither derives from the other. This is what errata 37 calls independence, in its strong form: the second implementation was EXECUTED, not read. C7 and C9 previously carried string literals copied out of the upstream test file, which pins what the reader believed the TypeScript would return rather than what it returns. Those literals are still carried, in crosscheck_typescript_expected, because they are the only check on the transcription itself -- but they are the floor and this is the standard.
oracle.domain: Every vector in group_c_addr.json. Until P3-3 the domain was every vector carrying a transcribed literal, which selected three of twenty-nine -- a fact about how many literals someone typed rather than about what the TypeScript can answer. Each vector is now classified by the fields it carries, and the dispatched and the explicitly excluded must together account for every vector in the file. The generator asserts that count and aborts on any vector matching neither.
oracle.not_an_oracle: The independent Python check on the addr_from_wots vector (ripemd160(sha3_512(x)) via hashlib) is NOT a third implementation and is deliberately not recorded as one. hashlib is the same two primitives in the same order, so it confirms the composition and nothing about the Mochimo-specific address construction around it.

vectors.note: EXECUTED CROSSCHECK of C7. addrTagToBase58 was called on the same 20-byte tag the C encoded, and its return value is recorded below. C7 in group_c_addr.json carries the same string as a literal read out of the upstream test file; both are kept, because the literal is the only thing that checks the transcription and the executed value is the only thing that checks the implementation.
vectors.falsifies: errata 37: the C's caller-applied CRC16 and the TypeScript checksum are the same scheme, established by executing the second implementation rather than by reading its test file
vectors.crc16_derivation: crc16 is not recomputed here. It is the checksum addrTagToBase58 itself appended, recovered by bs58-decoding that function’s output and reading bytes 20..21 little-endian (tag-utils.ts:13). crc() is not exported from the mochimo-wots package, so this reaches it through the boundary rather than around it.

vectors.note: EXECUTED CROSSCHECK of C6. addrFromWots was called on the exact bytes of C6_in.bin -- 2208 bytes, not WOTS_PK_LEN -- and returned null. The C has no such guard: it hashes whatever length it is given, which is why C6 exists as a negative control at all. The two implementations answer the same question differently and neither is wrong; recorded so the difference is visible rather than discovered later.
vectors.falsifies: that addr_from_wots is length-agnostic in both implementations. It is not: the TypeScript rejects any length but WOTS_PK_LEN, the C hashes what it is handed
